Write the actual property/relation and its actual arguments, never predicate/head placeholders or source IDs. Use lowercase adjectives or verbs (big, cold, kind, eats, needs, sees, visits, chases, likes), uppercase shared rule variables X for someone/they, Y for something/it, and quoted actual entities. Keep named subjects and objects as constants; a named dog or lion is not the variable X. Use a leading minus only for an actual not in that fragment. The source polarity hint is lexical, not a task answer. Do not turn a positive cold into -cold. Each rule has its own variable namespace. Use the full context to resolve an ellipsis. Do not output implication, conjunction, query markers, periods, comments or native answers inside a field. Earlier TRAIN examples use their own entities and source IDs; translate CURRENT fragments independently. In generic people/things rules (with or without All), every listed adjective and its conclusion use the same universal X.
